notes: Seeded detection corpus for the performance persona (2026-08-19 corpus-expansion). Same
self-contained-diff, AND-of-OR mustMatch grading evaluate-testing-charter.mjs already uses
for the testing, security and architecture corpora -- no code changes needed, only this
One defect fixture per Flag rule in the performance charter (N+1 query in a loop, quadratic
work over unbounded input, blocking sync I/O on a request path, unbounded cache growth,
loading a full dataset instead of paging), each paired with a near-miss clean control drawn
directly from the charter's own Do-not-flag list: a loop over a genuinely fixed/small config
collection, a cache that already has (or, in the diff, gains) real eviction, and a
per-row-query-in-a-loop shape that is a one-time backfill script rather than a request path.
The backfill control is deliberately the same surface shape as the N+1 defect fixture, to
test whether the lane is reading 'is this a request path' or just pattern-matching 'query
Run candidate-only (no charter rewrite here to A/B against a baseline snapshot):

fixtures.title: Load customer info alongside each order
fixtures.summary: A single batched customer lookup (WHERE id = ANY($1)) is replaced with one query per order inside a for-loop, turning a 2-query operation into 1+N queries that scales with the number of orders requested.

fixtures.title: Trim whitespace before deduping imported emails
fixtures.summary: The O(n) Set-based membership check is replaced with result.some(...) inside the loop, an O(n) scan per email that makes the whole dedupe O(n^2) -- on a bulk CSV import that can be tens of thousands of rows.

fixtures.title: Include the export file size in the response headers
fixtures.summary: fs.readFile/fs.promises is swapped for fs.readFileSync and fs.statSync inside an async Express handler, blocking the entire event loop -- and every other in-flight request -- for the duration of the disk read on every request to this route.

fixtures.title: Cache geocode lookups for the life of the process
fixtures.summary: A plain object cache keyed by user-supplied address strings is added with no eviction, no TTL and no maximum size, in a long-lived process -- it grows for as long as the process runs and as many distinct addresses as callers ever pass.

fixtures.title: Sort recent orders by total as a tiebreaker
fixtures.summary: LIMIT/OFFSET paging in the SQL is dropped in favour of fetching every order for the customer, sorting the full result set in application memory, and slicing the page out of it -- so response time and memory now scale with the customer's entire order history, not the page size.

fixtures.title: Add JPY to the supported currency list
fixtures.summary: Control: loadCurrencyRates loops over a hardcoded, small, fixed-by-construction currency list and calls the rates client once per entry -- this looks like the N+1 pattern on the surface (network call inside a loop) but the charter explicitly excludes collections that are fixed and small by construction, such as a config list. Adding one entry to that list does not change its character.

fixtures.title: Evict the oldest entry once the geocode cache is full
fixtures.summary: Control: this diff adds the missing eviction logic (a size check against the pre-existing MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES constant, deleting the oldest key) to what was already a bounded-intent cache. A reviewer that flags any cache.set() call as unbounded growth without reading the eviction guard right above it would false-positive here.

fixtures.title: Audit-log each region assignment during the customer backfill
fixtures.summary: Control: this adds a query-per-customer inside a loop -- the same surface shape as the N+1 defect fixture above -- but it is a one-time, manually-run backfill CLI script explicitly commented as not part of any request path. The charter excludes tooling and migrations from performance review because latency does not matter there.
